title: Reconstruction of the normalized finite smooth-purity tower
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth morphism of pure relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $n\geq1$ put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, let $A_{n,T}$ be its constant sheaf on $T$, and let $A_{n,T}(d)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}^{\otimes_{A_n}d}$ be the $d$-fold roots-of-unity twist [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf]. Form the strict semilinear towers $M_n=A_{n,X}(d)[2d]$ and $L_n=A_{n,Y}$, with transitions the quotient maps (and $u\mapsto u^\ell$ on roots of unity). The canonical reductions $M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,X}}A_{n,X}\cong M_n$ and $L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1,Y}}A_{n,Y}\cong L_n$ satisfy the quotient cocycle. Let $Rf_n^!$ and $\gamma_n=\gamma_{n,A_{n,Y}}:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$ be the finite constructible exceptional inverse image and the finite smooth-purity isomorphisms of [lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base], with its coefficient comparisons $c$ satisfying $c\circ(\gamma_{n+1}\otimes^L A_{n,X})=\gamma_n\circ\lambda$. Then the derived limits $M=R\varprojlim_nM_n$ and $L=R\varprojlim_nL_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] are objects of the completed integral constructible categories of $X$ and $Y$ with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their canonical reductions are $M_n$ and $L_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower, lem-weil-pbc-reconstruction-uniform-tower], and under these identifications the $\gamma_n$ identify the finite reductions of $M$ with the tower $(Rf_n^!L_n)_n$ and its coefficient comparisons. Every level is concentrated in degree $-2d$ on $X$ and degree $0$ on $Y$, with constructible cohomology, and the finite levels have compatible etale-origin witnesses.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text: Check the geometric and coefficient domains. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so the finite-type theorem makes $X,Y$ Noetherian. They have finite dimension: take finite affine covers by spectra of finite-type $k$-algebras. For each nonzero algebra, Noether normalization and its dimension theorem give a finite bound on prime-chain lengths. A chain of irreducible closed subsets of $T=X,Y$ restricts to a chain of the same length on any affine containing the generic point of its smallest member: this affine contains all generalizations of this point, including the distinct generic points of the other members. The maximum of the finitely many affine bounds bounds $\dim T$. Empty affine members are omitted. Since $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$, $\ell$ is a unit on $T$. Take $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$, $I=(\ell)$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. This DVR is Noetherian (a nonzero ideal is generated by an element of least valuation), $A/I^n=A_n$ is finite, $A/I$ is torsion, and the two-term free resolution $A\xrightarrow{\ell^n}A\to A_n$ proves the perfectness required by the adic datum. Thus the completed categories and reconstruction theorem are in their geometric and coefficient domains.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text:
Write $R_T=\varprojlim_n A_{n,T}$ and $Z_X=\varprojlim_n\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ with its root-power maps. The Tate-line lemma makes $Z_X$ an $R_X$-line. To identify its actual projections, clause 1 of the compatible-generator theorem supplies one pro-etale cover with primitive $\zeta_n$ and $\zeta_{n+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_n$. The sectionwise limit formula identifies $R_X$ with $Z_X$ on this cover by $(a_n)_n\mapsto(\zeta_n^{a_n})_n$, with inverse given by the coefficients in these generators. The $n$th projection is exactly $(a_r)_r\mapsto\zeta_n^{a_n}$. The completion-quotient theorem gives $R_X/\ell^nR_X=A_{n,X}$ (its Noetherian coefficient hypothesis was checked in Step 1). Thus the actual projection induces $Z_X\otimes_{R_X}A_{n,X}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X}$; these local isomorphisms are restrictions of that globally defined projection map.

Set $H_X=Z_X^{\otimes_{R_X}d}$, with $H_X=R_X$ at $d=0$, and $H_Y=R_Y$. They are lines on the same cover. Repeated balancing gives $H_X\otimes_{R_X}A_{n,X}\cong\mu_{\ell^n,X}^{\otimes_{A_{n,X}}d}$. For two factors use $(z\otimes w)\otimes a\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes(w\otimes a)$, with inverse $(z\otimes a)\otimes(w\otimes b)\mapsto(z\otimes w)\otimes ab$, and iterate. At $d=0$ use $r\otimes a\mapsto\pi_n(r)a$. The projection identity $\zeta_{n+1}^{\ell}=\zeta_n$ shows these quotient identifications respect the specified power transitions; on $Y$ they respect coefficient quotients.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text: The degree-zero lines just used are K-flat over their coefficient sheaves. Restrict an acyclic complex to a cover trivializing the line. Restriction is exact by the site-restriction lemma. Restriction also commutes with the sheaf tensor product: the presheaf tensors agree on objects $V\to U$, and for a sheaf $G$ on the slice the sheaf $(j_*G)(W)=G(W\times U)$ is right adjoint to restriction both for presheaves and for sheaves, so $\operatorname{Hom}(j^*(P^\#),G)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,j_*G)=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*P,G)=\operatorname{Hom}((j^*P)^\#,G)$ by the universal property of sheafification. Hence $(F\otimes H)|_U\cong F|_U\otimes H|_U$, and tensoring with the trivial line there is the identity by the tensor-unit maps, so the tensor complex is acyclic on each cover member. Its cohomology sheaves vanish globally by the sheaf axiom. This verifies the quantified definition of K-flatness. The same argument works at every finite level: clause 1 of the Tate-line lemma supplies etale trivializations of $\mu_{\ell^n}$, and their finite tensor powers and the constant line are trivial on those covers. Derived change of rings is therefore computed by the lines themselves. Consequently the ordinary quotient identifications of Step 2 are also the derived quotients with the same maps. The $[2d]$ shift merely shifts the tensor complex and preserves this computation.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text:
For $b\geq a\geq1$ the adjoint of the specified twist transition is the balanced map
$$(z_1\otimes\cdots\otimes z_d)\otimes t\longmapsto t\,(z_1^{\ell^{b-a}}\otimes\cdots\otimes z_d^{\ell^{b-a}})$$
from $A_{b,X}(d)\otimes_{A_{b,X}}A_{a,X}$ to $A_{a,X}(d)$. By Step 2 this is reduction of the single $R_X$-line $H_X$, hence locally the isomorphism $A_b\otimes_{A_b}A_a\cong A_a$, with inverse $t\mapsto1\otimes t$. Step 3 computes the derived tensor by that ordinary tensor. At $d=0$ the formula is $u\otimes t\mapsto q_{b,a}(u)t$, as on $Y$. For $c\geq b\geq a$, both reductions of $((h\otimes u)\otimes v)\otimes w$ give $h\otimes q_{c,a}(u)q_{b,a}(v)w$; the exponents on each root multiply to $\ell^{c-a}$. This proves the quotient cocycle including equal indices. With $[2d]$ on $X$, these are the normalizations of $M_\bullet,L_\bullet$. Restriction through $R_T\to A_{n,T}$ gives strict complexes of towers: all adjacent maps were defined on sheaves, before passage to derived categories.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text: Supply the uniform local models. Use the single stratum $T$ for $T=X,Y$. On the pro-etale cover trivializing $H_X$, take $H_X|_U[2d]$, and on $Y$ take $R_Y[0]$. Their terms are adic lisse of finite type: a trivial line is $\varprojlim_n\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n}$, the defining model with complete module $N=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and finite $N/\ell N=\mathbf F_\ell$. Their term bounds are $[-2d,-2d]$ and $[0,0]$. Steps 2-3 give quotient-linear isomorphisms $e_n$ from the finite levels to the reductions of these complexes. Step 4 gives exactly $e_n\rho_n=\sigma_n(e_{n+1}\otimes^L A_n)$. Their finite cohomology sheaves are locally constant with finite stalks: tensor the etale rank-one trivializations in clause 1 of the Tate-line lemma $d$ times, and use the constant line for $d=0$. Thus the finite-lisse condition holds at every level in the one stated degree. The same cover, stratum and local complex work for all $n$, which verifies every clause of the uniformly bounded constructible tower definition.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text:
Apply uniform-tower reconstruction to these towers with the local models of Step 5. Its finite-type hypothesis holds by Step 1. Its derived limit is the total right derived limit on the strict tower category, so it is exactly $M=R\varprojlim M_\bullet$ and $L=R\varprojlim L_\bullet$ in the statement. Reconstruction makes them derived $(\ell)$-complete and gives canonical projection-induced quotient-linear isomorphisms
$$M\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X}\cong M_n,\qquad L\otimes^L_{R_Y}A_{n,Y}\cong L_n,$$
compatible with normalization. Its equipped local comparisons exist explicitly here: the balanced maps of Step 2 and their inverses are maps of sheaves commuting with transitions, hence give strict tower isomorphisms to the local quotient models. Reconstruction also gives the single-degree bounds $[-2d,-2d]$ for $M$ and $[0,0]$ for $L$. All integral tensors are over $R_T$; no identification with the constant $\mathbf Z_\ell$ coefficient category is made.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text:
The finite-ring constructible-origin theorem applies to $M_n,L_n$: $A_n$ is finite, and Step 5 proves intrinsically constructible cohomology in one degree. Choose its bounded etale origins and comparison isomorphisms $\alpha_n$. Apply the normalized-etale-origin-witness theorem to those choices and the normalization isomorphisms $\rho_{b,a}$ of Step 4. Its hypotheses are bounded-below origins at each level and the quotient cocycle, already established. It supplies unique reduction isomorphisms $\beta_{b,a}$ with
$$\alpha_a\nu_T^*\beta_{b,a}=\rho_{b,a}(\alpha_b\otimes^L A_a),$$
and their unit and quotient cocycles. These are the compatible witnesses required by the completed integral constructible definition. The definition asks for these data on the coefficient-datum reductions $K_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}A_{n,X}$ with their normalization maps, not on $M_n$. Let $\kappa_n:K_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$ be the canonical isomorphisms of Step 6, which intertwine those normalizations with $\rho_{b,a}$. Then $\kappa_n^{-1}\alpha_n$ with the same $\beta_{b,a}$ are compatible witnesses for $K_\bullet$, and $e_n\kappa_n$ with the cover, stratum and local complex of Step 5 make $K_\bullet$ uniformly bounded constructible; both required equations follow by composing the displayed ones with the $\kappa$-square. The same holds for $L$. Together with derived completeness from Step 6, this proves membership of $M,L$ in those full subcategories. The arbitrary-finite-ring origin theorem introduces no finite-field or algebraic-closure hypothesis on $k$.

source.place: Steps 1-3: normalized finite tower, strict reconstruction and identification of finite reductions

proof.text:
Use the finite smooth-adjunction theorem with $K=A_{b,Y}$ and $A_b\to A_a$. The given smooth pure-dimensional morphism is between separated finite-type schemes over a field of characteristic different from $\ell$, and the constant $K$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Its twist identification $\lambda$ is the projection-induced normalization $\rho_{b,a}$ of Step 4. Its coefficient compatibility reads
$$c\circ(\gamma_b\otimes^L A_{a,X})=\gamma_a\circ\rho_{b,a}.$$
Compose with the canonical reductions of Step 6. This identifies the reductions of $M$ with $(Rf_n^!L_n)_n$, respecting its coefficient comparisons. The theorem's quotient cocycle for $c$ gives the same conclusion for all composite transitions. Each exceptional value is isomorphic by $\gamma_n$ to $M_n$, so its cohomology is constructible and vanishes outside degree $-2d$. Its compatible etale witnesses are those of $M_n$ from Step 7 with $\alpha_n$ followed by $\gamma_n$; the displayed square checks compatibility. The levels on $Y$ are in degree zero. This asserts the stated finite-tower identification without asserting an integral exceptional functor or a new map on derived limits.
